_comment: Public Turso configuration for the browser.
1. readToken — scoped to `drops:data_read`. Used by the user-facing
frontend to read the drop feed. Can only SELECT from the `drops` table.
2. writeToken — scoped to `drops:data_write`. Used by the admin-facing
frontend to create new drops. Can INSERT (and UPDATE/DELETE) into the
`drops` table. The token is public by design — any user can view the
JavaScript, but Turso enforces the scope server-side.
then create a new one and update this file, e.g.:
turso db tokens create lockdrop -p drops:data_read -e never
turso db tokens create lockdrop -p drops:data_read,data_add,data_update,data_delete -e never
Note: there is no `data_write` action. A write scope has to be spelled
out as data_add / data_update / data_delete, or the token is rejected
then push the updated `public/turso.json` to Cloudflare Pages.
then update this file and push.
